final.observation: Independent equipment and beam findings agree: a sustained beam disturbance began at 1604277200689428941–1604277200697686480 ns, and KLYS:LI29:11:AMPL recorded a near-zero amplitude update of 0.0244140625 at 1604277203201922048 ns followed by 69.091796875 at 1604277208198788864 ns. This corroborates an associated RF amplitude anomaly and beam disturbance, but sparse asynchronous reporting does not establish KLYS:LI29:11 as the unique cause.
supporting_evidence: KLYS:LI29:11:AMPL showed a 99.96467679265277% maximum absolute deviation from its 69.1162109375 time-weighted baseline median, with the near-zero update at 1604277203201922048 ns and a later 69.091796875 update [T-37ec9e46fff8].
Sustained low charge began at 1604277200697686480 ns in BPMS:DMPH:502:TMIT, BPMS:DMPH:693:TMIT, and BPMS:LTUH:450:TMIT [T-2c31c73f97c7].
Charge-qualified BPMS:LTUH:250:X showed a sustained 42-sample excursion beginning at 1604277200689428941 ns while BPMS:LTUH:250:TMIT remained above the low-charge criterion [T-f507fbefd015].
Timing analysis applied no timestamp shift and placed the clustered beam onsets before the recorded near-zero RF update [T-095069d88481].
conflicting_evidence: BPMS:LTUH:250:TMIT did not meet the sustained low-charge heuristic, so charge loss was not observed at every monitored BPM [T-2c31c73f97c7].

KLYS:LI29:11:AMPL was the sole suspicious RF channel among evaluable baselines, but 28 neighboring baselines were unknown; this is limited negative evidence and does not prove other stations were normal [T-adc89116ae80].
data_limitations: KLYS:LI29:11:AMPL had only 20 finite updates and a 0.9724137931034482 no-update fraction; sparse NaNs indicate no new update, and leading missing values remain unknown [T-37ec9e46fff8].
RF reporting is asynchronous, and the documented 0–5 s delay is approximate rather than a calibrated event-specific offset; no fixed delay or timestamp shift is inferred [T-095069d88481].
Low-charge position samples are invalid and were not used for orbit interpretation [T-f507fbefd015].
No RF phase data are available, neighboring records may be missing or inactive, and temporal association does not prove causation [T-095069d88481, T-adc89116ae80].

findings.observation: A beam disturbance is corroborated. Sustained low charge began near 1604277200697686480 ns at DMPH:502, DMPH:693, and LTUH:450, while LTUH:250 retained charge but showed a sustained X excursion beginning at 1604277200689428941 ns. The close beam-onset times identify a timing concern, but asynchronous RF reporting and the approximate 0–5 s reporting delay do not establish a fixed offset or a unique RF cause.
supporting_evidence: Three TMIT channels had 300–301 low-charge samples and sustained runs of 301 samples, first sustained at 1604277200697686480 ns (T-2c31c73f97c7).

conflicting_evidence: LTUH:250:TMIT had zero low-charge samples and peak robust z=5.3727, so charge loss was not observed at every monitored BPM (T-2c31c73f97c7).

DMPH:502:Y, DMPH:693:Y, and LTUH:450:X had 300, 301, and 300 invalid position samples respectively; their apparent position excursions are not valid beam-position evidence during low charge (T-f507fbefd015).
data_limitations: The disturbance heuristic is exploratory and is not a reproduction of the published detector (T-f507fbefd015).
RF observations are asynchronous; the documented reporting delay is only an approximate 0–5 s range, no timestamp shift was applied, and causal attribution is not established (T-095069d88481).
No RF phase data are available; sparse RF NaNs mean no new update, leading unknown values remain unknown, and neighboring station coverage may be incomplete (T-095069d88481).
findings.requested_next_check: Review charge-qualified LTUH:250:X samples around 1604277200689428941 ns against independently timestamped RF/interlock records, without applying a fixed timing shift; exclude all low-charge position samples.
